question_text: A government employee posts a critical comment about her supervisor on social media during office hours using a government computer. She is suspended for 30 days. She claims her freedom of speech was violated. Which of the following is the most likely outcome?

options.text: The suspension is valid because her speech was not protected as it was made during work hours using government property.
The suspension is invalid because freedom of speech is absolute and cannot be restricted.
The suspension is valid only if the comment was defamatory or obscene.
The suspension is invalid because she was exercising her right to criticize the government.
